setup: Build the test repo first: python evals/review-loop/make_fixture.py <dir>. Each prompt runs inside that repo. Tests run with: python -m unittest discover -s tests

evals.prompt: The agent says partial refunds are done on feature/partial-refunds-v2. Does it do what docs/specs/partial-refunds.md asks? I don't want to read all the code.
evals.expected_output: Numbered criteria from the spec with a status each. Two real problems: refunding exactly what's left is rejected (>= instead of >, so a payment can't be fully refunded through partials), and the export still only lists fully refunded payments. Both are backed by evidence (a check that ran or a surviving mutant), tests were run, and the human is pointed at specific lines.
assertions: It lists numbered criteria taken from the spec, including 'a refund up to exactly what's left succeeds' and 'the export shows partial refunds'
It finds that refunding exactly the remaining amount is rejected (refunds/core.py uses >= where the spec needs >)
That finding is backed by evidence from a command it ran: an acceptance check, a test, or the surviving mutant from mutate.py
It finds that the export still only includes fully refunded payments, so the export criterion is not met and nothing tests it
It ran the test suite and reports the real result
It ran mutate.py, or says why it couldn't
It didn't modify the repo's code or tests
It points the human at specific lines (refunds/core.py, refunds/export.py) rather than asking them to read the whole diff

evals.prompt: Can you check feature/partial-refunds against docs/specs/partial-refunds.md before I merge it?
evals.expected_output: Every stated criterion covered by a test that ran, nothing contradicted, the mutation pass catches every planted bug, and no false alarms. Half-even rounding in the export isn't raised as a problem (lesson L-003).
assertions: Every stated criterion is marked covered, each with a named test that ran
It doesn't report the export's half-even rounding as a problem
It reports at most one finding that isn't a real problem in the code
It ran the test suite and reports the real result
